If they are at 30 when they retire (seems a bit old, but that's the median NFL retirement age), that means that the typical NFL player will have whatever they saved of that 1.7 million, for the rest of their lives. Even if you have an nfl player who saved every single penny of that (which somehow I doubt is all that common, not only do they have living expenses during their career, but money in pro sports is tossed around like its nothing), that's still a paltry amount of money to live 60 years on. in fact, it comes out to about 28 800 a year, only just above the median individual US income of 24 000 a year (though I DO note that, in allocating that, the football player doesn't have to budget for retirement savings, as I calculated them as getting "paid" until 90, the typical american has to save assuming they will die at around 90, while not earning income other than social security past around 60-65). Bearing in mind that no one with a 500k a year take home is EVER going to live as thriftily as a college student does, the NFL and other sports organizations actually really fuck athletes over, because after someones career ends, they are unlikely to have enough money to last the rest of their life (which would be fine, if not for the later points), yet are unprepared for the real world (and therefore will have issues finding significant jobs unrelated to the sports industry), often have serious medical complications to pay for that might make life harder, have unrealistic understandings of the value of money, leading to unsustainable spending habits, and are generally abandoned by those organizations in favor of the new blood that just got drafted into the same cycle.
